$comment: Derives from CMC v0.9.15 at commit 6754d3c (github.com/Fraunhofer-AISEC/cmc). The pin governs more than the shapes below: 6754d3c is 'attestedtls: introduce new channel binding', which replaced the exporter-only report nonce with bindReportNonce = sha256(RFC 5705 exporter || prover TLS leaf cert), each side verifying the peer did the same (attestedtls/attestation.go). A task consuming this schema for the attested channel must implement that binding; the pre-6754d3c nonce is symmetric and reflectable.
title: Mock attestation sample (JSON)
description: One mock sample per CMC evidence type: the JSON shape that type of evidence takes, with the collateral that accompanies it. The 'evidence' and 'collateral' objects follow CMC's attestationreport types exactly (attestationreport.go, json.go); 'mock' and 'profile' belong to the sample wrapper, since CMC's own objects have no field to mark a mock.

base64.description: Standard base64, as Go's encoding/json writes []byte fields.

hex.description: Lowercase hex, as CMC's HexByte type writes itself (json.go).

EvidenceType.description: One sample per evidence type that a driver in cmcd's 'drivers' config emits as Evidence.type. Excluded, for different reasons: 'IAS Evidence', a real type no pinned driver emits; and IMA measurement lists, a software inventory carried in a 'PCR Eventlog' — not an evidence type, and 'ima' is a per-driver boolean, not a driver.

mock.description: Marks the sample as synthetic: no driver ran, no hardware was involved.

Evidence.description: The signed claim from one driver. CMC defines its payload as opaque bytes (e.g. an SNP report, a TPM quote, the sw JWS), so it is base64 here.

Collateral.description: What a verifier needs to check one evidence; matched to it by type. The sw driver supplies a public key; every hardware driver supplies a cert chain instead.

Component.description: One measurement. 'type' is a CycloneDX kind (firmware, operating-system, platform, application, data) or empty: the sgx/tdx drivers leave it empty on collateral entries.
